Hi Olivia,

Thanks for sending over Aurora's continuity questionnaire. Attached is our warm-standby focused response (PDF) plus a short runbook snippet that illustrates how we execute a partial-region warm-standby promotion with minimized cache-loss.

High-level assurances:
- RTO: targeted 5 minutes for control-plane failover signals; 15 minutes for full API enforcement across a promoted region for traffic-lawful endpoints (see page 3 of the PDF for conditional caveats).
- RPO: best-effort async replication with continuous KV checkpointing — typical RPO under normal replication is <30s for session metadata, up to 5 minutes for large-batch ingest depending on workload.
- Traffic cutover: can be automated with our routing policy engine or executed manually by Aurora ops.

Attachments: Redwood_WarmStandby_Response_20261028.pdf (answers + diagrams), supporting_runbook_snippet.txt (runbook excerpt).

If you need an architecture walkthrough, Marissa and Karthik are available for a call this week.

Hi Olivia — consolidated answers below for your reviewers and a draft SLA addendum attached (PDF). We also uploaded the runbook snippet and a runbook diagram to the Drive link in case your ops team wants direct access.

Answers (summary):
1) Partial-region RTO (control-plane vs enforcement)
- Control-plane failover (leader election, routing policy switch) is instrumented and typically completes within 1–5 minutes depending on the number of affected nodes and in-flight routing TTLs.
- Enforcement across client-facing API endpoints (rate-limiting propagation, cache warming, token-bucket recalibration) completes within a practical window usually under 15 minutes. During this window endpoints remain available; customers may see transient elevated latency (median +40–120ms depending on model size) until local caches warm. We recommend design patterns (short client-side retry backoff + idempotent request patterns) to minimize visible impact.

2) In-flight writes and data durability
- We employ ordered append logs with continuous checkpointing to a durable object store. For small session-level writes (metadata, short prompts) RPO is typically <30s; for large batched uploads the RPO is workload-dependent and can be up to 5 minutes in extreme cases.
- For contractual language: "Redwood will make commercially reasonable efforts to persist in-flight write operations prior to region promotion. In the event of partial data loss during failover, Redwood's recovery processes aim to restore service availability; remediation and data reconciliation commitments are documented in the attached SLA addendum." (See SLA addendum, section 2.1).

3) Orchestration handoff (API vs console)
- We provide a documented REST orchestration API that authorized Aurora tenants can call to initiate a warm-standby promotion. API call initiates a controlled promotion sequence, returns a promotion-job-id, and streams status events via webhook or polling.
- For Dedicated and VPC deployments we recommend API-triggered promotion; console/operator is supported for manual intervention and audit-friendly human approval flows.
- Implementation notes: no runbook code change required for standard Dedicated customers. For Aurora we can provide a short integration guide that includes example curl requests and webhook event schemas.

Attachments: WarmStandby_SLA_Addendum_aurora_draft.pdf (SLA language + remediation steps), runbook diagram & snippet (Drive link).

Next steps: If that language works for legal, I can send a DocuSign-ready version of the SLA addendum. Also proposing a 30-minute technical handover with your ops team to review the orchestration API next week — suggested slots are Mon/Tue mornings PT.
